questions: If the bottom row becomes completely filled after some blocks move downward during a time step, does the removal of that row happen before or after those blocks move?
When the entire bottom row is removed, are the blocks in that row deleted instantly at the start of the time step, or after all downward movements for that step have been processed?
If multiple blocks would move into the same cell during the same time step, is that situation possible, and if so, how should it be resolved?
Does the removal of the bottom row affect the “bottom row” definition for the remaining blocks within the same time step (i.e., does the next row become the new bottom row for further moves)?
Are blocks considered to exist at non-integer times only at the half‑step moments (e.g., T+0.5), and does the query ask about the state after the removal step but before any movement at time T+1?
Can the value of W be larger than the number of distinct X‑coordinates among the blocks, and if so, are empty columns simply ignored?

Is there any limit on the total number of time steps simulated (e.g., does the process stop earlier if all blocks are removed), or must we conceptually continue up to 10^100 regardless of block existence?
If a block is removed because its row was cleared, does it cease to exist for all future queries, even if the same (X, Y) coordinates could be re‑occupied by another block later?

inline_prompts: There is a grid with 10^9 rows and W columns. The cell at the x-th column from the left and the y-th row from the bottom is denoted by (x,y). There are N blocks. Each block is a 1 \times 1 square, and block i-th (1 \leq i \leq N) is located at cell (X_i,Y_i) at time 0. At times t=1,2,\dots,10^{100}, the blocks are moved according to the following rules: Related — bottom-to-top sequential processing bears on move/removal ordering. - If the entire bottom row is filled with blocks, then all blocks in the bottom row are removed. - For each remaining block, perform the following: - If the block is in the bottom row, or if there is a block in the cell immediately below it, do nothing. - Otherwise, move the block one cell downward. You are given Q queries. For the j-th query (1 \leq j \leq Q), answer whether block A_j exists at time T_j+0.5. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N W X_1 Y_1 X_2 Y_2 \vdots X_N Y_N Q T_1 A_1 T_2 A_2 \vdots T_Q A_Q Output Print Q lines. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq W \leq N - 1 \leq X_i \leq W - 1 \leq Y_i \leq 10^9 - (X_i,Y_i) \neq (X_j,Y_j) if i \neq j. - 1 \leq Q \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq T_j \leq 10^9 - 1 \leq A_j \leq N - All input values are integers.
